To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we report the coincidence of CJD in 2 unrelated schoolteachers who were coworkers in the same school wing for 6 months, and that the first teacher developed ataxia and tremulousness 5 months after contact with his colleague, with a diagnosis of CJD made 2 months after onset of symptoms by brain biopsy.

1) the first teacher had an atypical form of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, 2) he developed ataxia and dementia 5 mo after last contact with his coworker, 3) he was diagnosed with CJD by brain biopsy 2 mo later, 4) the second teacher developed ataxia 8 mo after the first teacher was diagnosed and died of CJD 9 mo later, 5) the first teacher was the source of infection
